Title: Extreme weather as an occupational hazard: Structural vulnerability among multilingual immigrant workers
Proposed Project Title: A Weather-Ready Nation Para Todos: Evaluating Current Practices in Communicating Hazardous Weather Risks to Spanish Speakers
Suggested Parent Project: A Weather-Ready Nation Para Todos: Evaluating Current Practices in Communicating Hazardous Weather Risks to Spanish Speakers
Authors / PI: Elisabet De Jesús-Otero; Joseph E. Trujillo-Falcón; Anthony L. Corrales; América R. Gaviria Pabón; Samuel T. Halvorson; Salvatore Callesano; Liam E. Llewellyn; Eduardo Muñoz Suárez
Brief Abstract: Drawing on seven focus groups with 29 Spanish-speaking immigrant workers in Wichita and Garden City, Kansas, this article examines structural barriers to workplace safety during extreme weather. Participants described limited multilingual risk information, inconsistent emergency procedures, fear of workplace retaliation, and commuting or caregiving obligations that constrained protective action. The authors identify organizational preparedness, accessible multilingual warnings, and weather-resilient workplace practices as important ways to reduce vulnerability.
